facts.text: The repository is a reinforcement-learning framework based on NVIDIA Isaac Gym for humanoid locomotion that also integrates a sim-to-sim framework from Isaac Gym to MuJoCo
The README documents the MuJoCo sim-to-sim run as python scripts/sim2sim.py --load_model /path/to/export/model.pt
setup.py declares isaacgym (preview4), mujoco==2.3.6 and mujoco-python-viewer in install_requires
run_mujoco(policy, cfg) is the MuJoCo simulation loop
run_mujoco loads the MJCF with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path(cfg.sim_config.mujoco_model_path), overwrites model.opt.timestep with cfg.sim_config.dt, creates MjData and calls mujoco.mj_step
get_obs reads the orientation sensor (reordered to x, y, z, w) and the angular-velocity sensor
Sim2simCfg selects resources/robots/XBot/mjcf/XBot-L-terrain.xml only with --terrain and resources/robots/XBot/mjcf/XBot-L.xml otherwise
Sim2simCfg sets sim_duration 60 s, dt 0.001 s and decimation 10
The loop computes PD torques, clips them to cfg.robot_config.tau_limit, writes them to data.ctrl and advances the model with mujoco.mj_step
Sim2simCfg sets tau_limit to 200 for all twelve joints
The MJCF root element declares the model XBot-L
The model uses radians, resolves its meshes from ../meshes/, and its option element sets timestep 0.001 s, 50 solver iterations, the PGS solver and gravity 0 0 -9.81
The world contains a plane ground and a base_link body at 0 0 0.88 that carries three slide joints and one ball joint
The left leg chain has six limited hinge joints, left_leg_roll_joint through left_ankle_roll_joint, each with its own range
The right leg chain has six limited hinge joints, right_leg_roll_joint through right_ankle_roll_joint, each with its own range
The actuator section declares twelve motor actuators, one per leg hinge, each with ctrllimited true and ctrlrange -200 200

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the fixed model deterministically from the model defaults; the bridge accepts a seed in cap.world.reset.v1 but a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults and does not use it, so one control sequence repeats a trajectory on the same engine.  The package's stand-in is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the MJCF for the three base slides, the base ball joint, the twelve actuated leg hinges, their explicit ctrlranges and the 0.001 s option step, then gives each actuated hinge a placeholder velocity proportional to its control value and holds the base where the model puts it; it computes no inertia, torque, gravity, contact, friction, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics and produces no MuJoCo trajectory
the stand-in loads no STL mesh or texture and resolves no collision or contact; the model's ground plane, base collision geoms and armature attributes are not applied

the upstream sim2sim loop overwrites the model step with its own 0.001 s dt (the same value the MJCF states), computes PD torques from a TorchScript policy and writes them to data.ctrl; this package does not run that loop and takes the control vector directly from the caller

the upstream loop also builds its observation from the orientation and angular-velocity sensors, the joint arrays and the previous action; this package publishes the bridge's world state instead and does not model those sensors
the fake reset restores the parsed model qpos0 and zeros; a real MjData reset also restores the full integration state, which this package did not inspect
the real mujoco path (a backend name that backends does not list) was not run for this package, so no trajectory was compared with the engine and no physical XBot-L was involved

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
